blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.

blocks.text:
name: 'Mirror checkout (self-hosted)'
description: >-
  The shared self-hosted mirror-checkout for the macOS publish legs
  (build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos):
  clone the repo into $GITHUB_WORKSPACE from the persistent local git
  mirror. gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on a persistent self-hosted runner is
  SHARED across workflow runs — bench-harbor used to park jobs/<run-id>/
  (trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers) in it, and the old bare
  `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` exited 1 on the unremovable leftovers,
  failing the checkout before any build step. The clean is now
  log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder
  into $RUNNER_TEMP, and as a last resort clone into a sibling directory
  and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can
  no longer fail the checkout. (The root cause moved the bench output
  outside the workspace: bench-harbor.yml now writes
  $RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs; this tolerance covers stale leftovers and any
  future leak.)

inputs:
  repo-url:
    description: 'Repository URL cloned from the local mirror'
    required: false
    default: 'https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git'
  preserve-path:
    description: >-
      Workspace-relative path preserved across the clean (parked in
      preserve-cache-dir before the clean, restored after the clone) —
      e.g. build-macos''s per-arch build cache
    required: false
    default: ''
  preserve-cache-dir:
    description: 'Directory the preserved path is parked in (required when preserve-path is set; $HOME expands at run time)'
    required: false
    default: ''

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Clean workspace (gh-1600 log-and-prune) and clone from the local mirror
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        REPO_URL='${{ inputs.repo-url }}'
        MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/$(basename "$REPO_URL")"
        PRESERVE='${{ inputs.preserve-path }}'
        CACHE='${{ inputs.preserve-cache-dir }}'
        cd /tmp
        echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

        # Park the preserved path (per-arch build cache) outside the
        # workspace first — the clean below removes everything else.
        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ]; then
          SRC="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$PRESERVE"
          if [ -d "$SRC" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing $PRESERVE in $CACHE..."
            rm -rf "$CACHE"
            mkdir -p "$CACHE"
            mv "$SRC" "$CACHE/"
          fi
        fi

        # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
        # shared workspace (bench leftovers held by docker containers) —
        # log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
        if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
        fi
        if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
          if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
          fi
        fi
        mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

        CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a live
          # bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build the
          # checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A bench
          # leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path; if one
          # ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 "$REPO_URL" "$CLONE_TARGET"
        if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
          while IFS= read -r entry; do
            name="$(basename "$entry")"
            if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
              echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
            else
              mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
            fi
          done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ] && [ -d "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" ]; then
          echo "Restoring $PRESERVE from $CACHE..."
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")"
          mv "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")/"
        fi

blocks.text:
I found a latent bug: `CACHE='${{ inputs.preserve-cache-dir }}'` — build-macos.yml passes `'$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-arm64'` and the input's own description promises "$HOME expands at run time", but bash single quotes mean NO expansion: `CACHE` holds the literal string `$HOME/...`. `mkdir -p "$CACHE"` creates `/tmp/$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/...` (a literal `$HOME` directory under /tmp), leaking junk and defeating the documented per-arch cache location.

Wait, let me double check bash semantics: `CACHE='$HOME/x'` assigns literal `$HOME/x`. Then `mkdir -p "$CACHE"` → creates path literally named `$HOME/x` relative to cwd. Yes, no expansion. Confirmed bug.

Fix options:
1. In the action: `CACHE="${CACHE/\$HOME/$HOME}"` — replaces first literal `$HOME` occurrence. Clean, one line, bash-only.
2. Or change build-macos.yml to expand: use env: block with `BUILD_CACHE_DIR: ${{ ... }}`... can't do `$HOME` in GH expressions. Could use `env: HOME_DIR: $HOME` no — GH env values support `$HOME`? In a workflow `env:` block, values are literal strings; `$HOME` would only expand when used unquoted in shell. The cleanest place is the action script: expand the literal `$HOME` token after assignment.

Also check the test asserts: contains('stale-workspace'), contains(r'rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true'), contains('git clone --reference'). My one-line addition doesn't affect those.

Also, description says "(required when preserve-path is set; $HOME expands at run time)" — after the fix that becomes true.

Another check on build-macos.yml — let me read the current state around the checkout step and verify the whole file parses and there are no leftover references to `$ARCH`/`BUILD_CACHE_DIR` that are now unused, and that matrix.arch is still used elsewhere. Also check the `MIRROR_BASE`/`update_mirror` step is intact.

Then also review build-mobile.yml and bench-harbor.yml current state fully (the diff showed them, but let me sanity check the file parses as YAML).

Plan:
1. Fix the `$HOME` expansion bug in the action (with test coverage? The test is static YAML-shape; I could add an assert that the action expands `$HOME` for preserve-cache-dir — i.e. contains `'${CACHE/\$HOME/$HOME}'`... a bit awkward but doable: `contains(r'CACHE="${CACHE/\$HOME/$HOME}"')`.)
2. Validate YAML of all touched files.

- `Build iOS IPA` executed on a **Linux** self-hosted runner (`/home/runner/…`; later steps fail with `security: command not found`). The 2026-10-14 signature (`exit 127` at *Install fastlane*) is the same routing bug — no ruby/fastlane on that box.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

+name: 'Mirror checkout (self-hosted)'
+description: >-
+  The shared self-hosted mirror-checkout for the macOS publish legs
+  (build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos):
+  clone the repo into $GITHUB_WORKSPACE from the persistent local git
+  mirror. gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on a persistent self-hosted runner is
+  SHARED across workflow runs — bench-harbor used to park jobs/<run-id>/
+  (trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers) in it, and the old bare
+  `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` exited 1 on the unremovable leftovers,
+  failing the checkout before any build step. The clean is now
+  log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder
+  into $RUNNER_TEMP, and as a last resort clone into a sibling directory
+  and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can
+  no longer fail the checkout. (The root cause moved the bench output
+  outside the workspace: bench-harbor.yml now writes
+  $RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs; this tolerance covers stale leftovers and any
+  future leak.)
+
+inputs:
+  repo-url:
+    description: 'Repository URL cloned from the local mirror'
+    required: false
+    default: 'https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git'
+  preserve-path:
+    description: >-
+      Workspace-relative path preserved across the clean (parked in
+      preserve-cache-dir before the clean, restored after the clone) —
+      e.g. build-macos''s per-arch build cache
+    required: false
+    default: ''
+  preserve-cache-dir:
+    description: 'Directory the preserved path is parked in (required when preserve-path is set; $HOME expands at run time)'
+    required: false
+    default: ''
+
+runs:
+  using: 'composite'
+  steps:
+    - name: Clean workspace (gh-1600 log-and-prune) and clone from the local mirror
+      shell: bash
+      run: |
+        set -euo pipefail
+        REPO_URL='${{ inputs.repo-url }}'
+        MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/$(basename "$REPO_URL")"
+        PRESERVE='${{ inputs.preserve-path }}'
+        CACHE='${{ inputs.preserve-cache-dir }}'
+        cd /tmp
+        echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
+        echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"
+
+        # Park the preserved path (per-arch build cache) outside the
+        # workspace first — the clean below removes everything else.
+        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ]; then
+          SRC="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$PRESERVE"
+          if [ -d "$SRC" ]; then
+            echo "Preserving existing $PRESERVE in $CACHE..."
+            rm -rf "$CACHE"
+            mkdir -p "$CACHE"
+            mv "$SRC" "$CACHE/"
+          fi

+        # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
+        # shared workspace (bench leftovers held by docker containers) —
+        # log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
+        if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
+          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
+          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
+        fi
+        if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
+          STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
+          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
+          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
+          if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
+            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
+          fi
+        fi
+        mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
+
+        CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
+        if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
+          # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a live
+          # bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build the
+          # checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A bench
+          # leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path; if one
+          # ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
+          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
+          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
+        fi
+        git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 "$REPO_URL" "$CLONE_TARGET"

+            fi
+          done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)

+        fi
+        echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"
+
+        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ] && [ -d "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" ]; then

+          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")"
+          mv "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")/"
+        fi

Variable contents are NOT re-expanded when referenced. `CACHE='$HOME/x'` → CACHE is literally `$HOME/x`; `"$CACHE"` → literally `$HOME/x`. `mv "$SRC" "$CACHE/"` would try to move into a directory literally named `$HOME` (relative `./$HOME/...`).

blocks.text:
name: 'Mirror checkout (self-hosted)'
description: >-
  The shared self-hosted mirror-checkout for the macOS publish legs
  (build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos):
  clone the repo into $GITHUB_WORKSPACE from the persistent local git
  mirror. gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on a persistent self-hosted runner is
  SHARED across workflow runs — bench-harbor used to park jobs/<run-id>/
  (trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers) in it, and the old bare
  `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` exited 1 on the unremovable leftovers,
  failing the checkout before any build step. The clean is now
  log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder
  into $RUNNER_TEMP, and as a last resort clone into a sibling directory
  and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can
  no longer fail the checkout. (The root cause moved the bench output
  outside the workspace: bench-harbor.yml now writes
  $RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs; this tolerance covers stale leftovers and any
  future leak.)

inputs:
  repo-url:
    description: 'Repository URL cloned from the local mirror'
    required: false
    default: 'https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git'
  preserve-path:
    description: >-
      Workspace-relative path preserved across the clean (parked in
      preserve-cache-dir before the clean, restored after the clone) —
      e.g. build-macos''s per-arch build cache
    required: false
    default: ''
  preserve-cache-dir:
    description: 'Directory the preserved path is parked in (required when preserve-path is set; $HOME expands at run time)'
    required: false
    default: ''

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Clean workspace (gh-1600 log-and-prune) and clone from the local mirror
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        REPO_URL='${{ inputs.repo-url }}'
        MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/$(basename "$REPO_URL")"
        PRESERVE='${{ inputs.preserve-path }}'
        CACHE='${{ inputs.preserve-cache-dir }}'
        cd /tmp
        echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

        # Park the preserved path (per-arch build cache) outside the
        # workspace first — the clean below removes everything else.
        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ]; then
          SRC="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$PRESERVE"
          if [ -d "$SRC" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing $PRESERVE in $CACHE..."
            rm -rf "$CACHE"
            mkdir -p "$CACHE"
            mv "$SRC" "$CACHE/"
          fi
        fi

        # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
        # shared workspace (bench leftovers held by docker containers) —
        # log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
        if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
        fi
        if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
          if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
          fi
        fi
        mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

        CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a live
          # bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build the
          # checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A bench
          # leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path; if one
          # ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 "$REPO_URL" "$CLONE_TARGET"
        if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
          while IFS= read -r entry; do
            name="$(basename "$entry")"
            if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
              echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
            else
              mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
            fi
          done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ] && [ -d "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" ]; then
          echo "Restoring $PRESERVE from $CACHE..."
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")"
          mv "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")/"
        fi

## Description

## RCA + fix plan (2026-10-15, night run 38686767148) — two independent failure layers

*No duplicate work in flight (checked 2026-10-15): no open PR touches build-mobile / daily-publish / fastlane (#1595 is an unmerged deps bump, #1566 is the pubdev leg).*

### L1 — TestFlight leg: mobile jobs route to a LINUX runner + shared workspace polluted by bench leftovers
- `Build iOS IPA` executed on a **Linux** self-hosted runner (`/home/runner/…`; later steps fail with `security: command not found`). The 2026-10-14 signature (`exit 127` at *Install fastlane*) is the same routing bug — no ruby/fastlane on that box.
- Immediate trigger tonight: the custom mirror-checkout runs `rm -rf $GITHUB_WORKSPACE`, which cannot remove **bench leftovers** — `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/` (sqlite files created/held by bench docker containers sharing the same workspace path) → `rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:

# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:

    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
---
  # passes, like every other optional leg).

  # `shared`-only diffs too — the classifier maps a shared/unknown path to
  # ALL nine stages, `test-core` among them, so `core=true` falls out and
  # this leg runs; only docs-only diffs (or non-PR context mismatches)
  # skip it.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    name: Cube kernel live (macOS)

    permissions:

    steps:

---

blocks.text:
name: 'Mirror checkout (self-hosted)'
description: >-
  The shared self-hosted mirror-checkout for the macOS publish legs
  (build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos):
  clone the repo into $GITHUB_WORKSPACE from the persistent local git
  mirror. gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on a persistent self-hosted runner is
  SHARED across workflow runs — bench-harbor used to park jobs/<run-id>/
  (trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers) in it, and the old bare
  `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` exited 1 on the unremovable leftovers,
  failing the checkout before any build step. The clean is now
  log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder
  into $RUNNER_TEMP, and as a last resort clone into a sibling directory
  and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can
  no longer fail the checkout. (The root cause moved the bench output
  outside the workspace: bench-harbor.yml now writes
  $RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs; this tolerance covers stale leftovers and any
  future leak.)

inputs:
  repo-url:
    description: 'Repository URL cloned from the local mirror'
    required: false
    default: 'https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git'
  preserve-path:
    description: >-
      Workspace-relative path preserved across the clean (parked in
      preserve-cache-dir before the clean, restored after the clone) —
      e.g. build-macos''s per-arch build cache
    required: false
    default: ''
  preserve-cache-dir:
    description: 'Directory the preserved path is parked in (required when preserve-path is set; $HOME expands at run time)'
    required: false
    default: ''

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Clean workspace (gh-1600 log-and-prune) and clone from the local mirror
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        REPO_URL='${{ inputs.repo-url }}'
        MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/$(basename "$REPO_URL")"
        PRESERVE='${{ inputs.preserve-path }}'
        CACHE='${{ inputs.preserve-cache-dir }}'
        cd /tmp
        echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

        # Park the preserved path (per-arch build cache) outside the
        # workspace first — the clean below removes everything else.
        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ]; then
          SRC="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$PRESERVE"
          if [ -d "$SRC" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing $PRESERVE in $CACHE..."
            rm -rf "$CACHE"
            mkdir -p "$CACHE"
            mv "$SRC" "$CACHE/"
          fi
        fi

        # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
        # shared workspace (bench leftovers held by docker containers) —
        # log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
        if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
        fi
        if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
          if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
          fi
        fi
        mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

        CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a live
          # bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build the
          # checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A bench
          # leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path; if one
          # ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 "$REPO_URL" "$CLONE_TARGET"
        if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
          while IFS= read -r entry; do
            name="$(basename "$entry")"
            if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
              echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
            else
              mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
            fi
          done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ] && [ -d "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" ]; then
          echo "Restoring $PRESERVE from $CACHE..."
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")"
          mv "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")/"
        fi

# gh-1600: [daily-publish] testflight leg failed

## Description

## RCA + fix plan (2026-10-15, night run 38686767148) — two independent failure layers

*No duplicate work in flight (checked 2026-10-15): no open PR touches build-mobile / daily-publish / fastlane (#1595 is an unmerged deps bump, #1566 is the pubdev leg).*

### L1 — TestFlight leg: mobile jobs route to a LINUX runner + shared workspace polluted by bench leftovers
- `Build iOS IPA` executed on a **Linux** self-hosted runner (`/home/runner/…`; later steps fail with `security: command not found`). The 2026-10-14 signature (`exit 127` at *Install fastlane*) is the same routing bug — no ruby/fastlane on that box.
- Immediate trigger tonight: the custom mirror-checkout runs `rm -rf $GITHUB_WORKSPACE`, which cannot remove **bench leftovers** — `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/` (sqlite files created/held by bench docker containers sharing the same workspace path) → `rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1.
- So: iOS on Linux was never going to pass (routing), and bench writing into the build workspace would break checkouts even on macOS (isolation).

### L2 — CLI leg: fa-extension.zip size budget regression (+5.0% gate)
- Tracked class **#1262** (bundle grew after the Oct-14 merge wave). This leg blocks the publish independently of TestFlight.

## Fix plan

- **F-A (routing):** mobile/iOS jobs in `build-mobile.yml` pin the macOS runner label explicitly — `runs-on: fa-m5-1` (the repo's ONE self-hosted macOS M5 runner) — and must not match generic `self-hosted` labels advertised by the Linux box. Audit other macOS-only legs the same way.
- **F-B (workspace isolation):** the bench pipeline writes `jobs/<run-id>/` OUTSIDE the build workspace root (e.g. `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/<run-id>`); post-run cleanup tears docker containers down before rm; the mirror-checkout tolerates stale unremovable paths (log-and-prune) instead of failing the checkout.
- **F-C (size budget):** out of scope here — **#1262**; this publish stays red until the bundle shrinks or the baseline is renegotiated there.

## Acceptance
- **AC1** — `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` execute on `fa-m5-1` (runner name in job annotations), never on Linux; REG: workflow-lint asserts mobile jobs' `runs-on` carries the macOS label.

- **AC3** — next scheduled `daily-publish` is green for TestFlight + CLI legs (L2/#1262 permitting) and a TestFlight build actually ships.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

@@ -0,0 +1,108 @@
+name: 'Mirror checkout (self-hosted)'
+description: >-
+  The shared self-hosted mirror-checkout for the macOS publish legs
+  (build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos):
+  clone the repo into $GITHUB_WORKSPACE from the persistent local git
+  mirror. gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on a persistent self-hosted runner is
+  SHARED across workflow runs — bench-harbor used to park jobs/<run-id>/
+  (trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers) in it, and the old bare
+  `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` exited 1 on the unremovable leftovers,
+  failing the checkout before any build step. The clean is now
+  log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder
+  into $RUNNER_TEMP, and as a last resort clone into a sibling directory
+  and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can
+  no longer fail the checkout. (The root cause moved the bench output
+  outside the workspace: bench-harbor.yml now writes
+  $RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs; this tolerance covers stale leftovers and any
+  future leak.)
+
+inputs:
+  repo-url:
+    description: 'Repository URL cloned from the local mirror'
+    required: false
+    default: 'https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git'
+  preserve-path:
+    description: >-
+      Workspace-relative path preserved across the clean (parked in
+      preserve-cache-dir before the clean, restored after the clone) —
+      e.g. build-macos''s per-arch build cache
+    required: false
+    default: ''
+  preserve-cache-dir:
+    description: 'Directory the preserved path is parked in (required when preserve-path is set; $HOME expands at run time)'
+    required: false
+    default: ''
+
+runs:
+  using: 'composite'
+  steps:
+    - name: Clean workspace (gh-1600 log-and-prune) and clone from the local mirror
+      shell: bash
+      run: |
+        set -euo pipefail
+        REPO_URL='${{ inputs.repo-url }}'
+        MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/$(basename "$REPO_URL")"
+        PRESERVE='${{ inputs.preserve-path }}'
+        CACHE='${{ inputs.preserve-cache-dir }}'
+        cd /tmp
+        echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
+        echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"
+
+        # Park the preserved path (per-arch build cache) outside the
+        # workspace first — the clean below removes everything else.
+        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ]; then
+          SRC="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$PRESERVE"
+          if [ -d "$SRC" ]; then
+            echo "Preserving existing $PRESERVE in $CACHE..."
+            rm -rf "$CACHE"
+            mkdir -p "$CACHE"
+            mv "$SRC" "$CACHE/"
+          fi
+        fi
+
+        # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
+        # shared workspace (bench leftovers held by docker containers) —
+        # log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
+        if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
+          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
+          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
+        fi
+        if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
+          STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
+          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
+          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
+          if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
+            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
+          fi
+        fi
+        mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
+
+        CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
+        if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
+          # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a live
+          # bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build the
+          # checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A bench
+          # leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path; if one
+          # ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
+          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
+          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
+        fi
+        git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 "$REPO_URL" "$CLONE_TARGET"
+        if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
+          while IFS= read -r entry; do
+            name="$(basename "$entry")"
+            if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then

+            else
+              mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
+            fi
+          done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
+          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
+        fi
+        echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"
+
+        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ] && [ -d "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" ]; then
+          echo "Restoring $PRESERVE from $CACHE..."
+          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")"
+          mv "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")/"
+        fi

blocks.text:
name: 'Mirror checkout (self-hosted)'
description: >-
  The shared self-hosted mirror-checkout for the macOS publish legs
  (build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos):
  clone the repo into $GITHUB_WORKSPACE from the persistent local git
  mirror. gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on a persistent self-hosted runner is
  SHARED across workflow runs — bench-harbor used to park jobs/<run-id>/
  (trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers) in it, and the old bare
  `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` exited 1 on the unremovable leftovers,
  failing the checkout before any build step. The clean is now
  log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder
  into $RUNNER_TEMP, and as a last resort clone into a sibling directory
  and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can
  no longer fail the checkout. (The root cause moved the bench output
  outside the workspace: bench-harbor.yml now writes
  $RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs; this tolerance covers stale leftovers and any
  future leak.)

inputs:
  repo-url:
    description: 'Repository URL cloned from the local mirror'
    required: false
    default: 'https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git'
  preserve-path:
    description: >-
      Workspace-relative path preserved across the clean (parked in
      preserve-cache-dir before the clean, restored after the clone) —
      e.g. build-macos''s per-arch build cache
    required: false
    default: ''
  preserve-cache-dir:
    description: 'Directory the preserved path is parked in (required when preserve-path is set; $HOME expands at run time)'
    required: false
    default: ''

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Clean workspace (gh-1600 log-and-prune) and clone from the local mirror
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        REPO_URL='${{ inputs.repo-url }}'
        MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/$(basename "$REPO_URL")"
        PRESERVE='${{ inputs.preserve-path }}'
        CACHE='${{ inputs.preserve-cache-dir }}'
        cd /tmp
        echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

        # Park the preserved path (per-arch build cache) outside the
        # workspace first — the clean below removes everything else.
        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ]; then
          SRC="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$PRESERVE"
          if [ -d "$SRC" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing $PRESERVE in $CACHE..."
            rm -rf "$CACHE"
            mkdir -p "$CACHE"
            mv "$SRC" "$CACHE/"
          fi
        fi

        # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
        # shared workspace (bench leftovers held by docker containers) —
        # log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
        if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
        fi
        if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
          if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
          fi
        fi
        mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

        CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a live
          # bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build the
          # checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A bench
          # leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path; if one
          # ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 "$REPO_URL" "$CLONE_TARGET"
        if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
          while IFS= read -r entry; do
            name="$(basename "$entry")"
            if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
              echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
            else
              mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
            fi
          done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ] && [ -d "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" ]; then
          echo "Restoring $PRESERVE from $CACHE..."
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")"
          mv "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")/"
        fi

# gh-1600: [daily-publish] testflight leg failed

## Description

## RCA + fix plan (2026-10-15, night run 38686767148) — two independent failure layers

*No duplicate work in flight (checked 2026-10-15): no open PR touches build-mobile / daily-publish / fastlane (#1595 is an unmerged deps bump, #1566 is the pubdev leg).*

### L1 — TestFlight leg: mobile jobs route to a LINUX runner + shared workspace polluted by bench leftovers
- `Build iOS IPA` executed on a **Linux** self-hosted runner (`/home/runner/…`; later steps fail with `security: command not found`). The 2026-10-14 signature (`exit 127` at *Install fastlane*) is the same routing bug — no ruby/fastlane on that box.
- Immediate trigger tonight: the custom mirror-checkout runs `rm -rf $GITHUB_WORKSPACE`, which cannot remove **bench leftovers** — `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/` (sqlite files created/held by bench docker containers sharing the same workspace path) → `rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1.
- So: iOS on Linux was never going to pass (routing), and bench writing into the build workspace would break checkouts even on macOS (isolation).

### L2 — CLI leg: fa-extension.zip size budget regression (+5.0% gate)
- Tracked class **#1262** (bundle grew after the Oct-14 merge wave). This leg blocks the publish independently of TestFlight.

## Fix plan

- **F-A (routing):** mobile/iOS jobs in `build-mobile.yml` pin the macOS runner label explicitly — `runs-on: fa-m5-1` (the repo's ONE self-hosted macOS M5 runner) — and must not match generic `self-hosted` labels advertised by the Linux box. Audit other macOS-only legs the same way.
- **F-B (workspace isolation):** the bench pipeline writes `jobs/<run-id>/` OUTSIDE the build workspace root (e.g. `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/<run-id>`); post-run cleanup tears docker containers down before rm; the mirror-checkout tolerates stale unremovable paths (log-and-prune) instead of failing the checkout.
- **F-C (size budget):** out of scope here — **#1262**; this publish stays red until the bundle shrinks or the baseline is renegotiated there.

## Acceptance
- **AC1** — `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` execute on `fa-m5-1` (runner name in job annotations), never on Linux; REG: workflow-lint asserts mobile jobs' `runs-on` carries the macOS label.
- **AC2** — bench run immediately followed by a mobile build on the same box: checkout succeeds; bench leftovers live outside `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` or are docker-torn-down first.
- **AC3** — next scheduled `daily-publish` is green for TestFlight + CLI legs (L2/#1262 permitting) and a TestFlight build actually ships.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name

blocks.text:
name: 'Mirror checkout (self-hosted)'
description: >-
  The shared self-hosted mirror-checkout for the macOS publish legs
  (build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos):
  clone the repo into $GITHUB_WORKSPACE from the persistent local git
  mirror. gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on a persistent self-hosted runner is
  SHARED across workflow runs — bench-harbor used to park jobs/<run-id>/
  (trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers) in it, and the old bare
  `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` exited 1 on the unremovable leftovers,
  failing the checkout before any build step. The clean is now
  log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder
  into $RUNNER_TEMP, and as a last resort clone into a sibling directory
  and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can
  no longer fail the checkout. (The root cause moved the bench output
  outside the workspace: bench-harbor.yml now writes
  $RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs; this tolerance covers stale leftovers and any
  future leak.)

inputs:
  repo-url:
    description: 'Repository URL cloned from the local mirror'
    required: false
    default: 'https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git'
  preserve-path:
    description: >-
      Workspace-relative path preserved across the clean (parked in
      preserve-cache-dir before the clean, restored after the clone) —
      e.g. build-macos''s per-arch build cache
    required: false
    default: ''
  preserve-cache-dir:
    description: 'Directory the preserved path is parked in (required when preserve-path is set; $HOME expands at run time)'
    required: false
    default: ''

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Clean workspace (gh-1600 log-and-prune) and clone from the local mirror
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        REPO_URL='${{ inputs.repo-url }}'
        MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/$(basename "$REPO_URL")"
        PRESERVE='${{ inputs.preserve-path }}'
        CACHE='${{ inputs.preserve-cache-dir }}'
        cd /tmp
        echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

        # Park the preserved path (per-arch build cache) outside the
        # workspace first — the clean below removes everything else.
        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ]; then
          SRC="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$PRESERVE"
          if [ -d "$SRC" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing $PRESERVE in $CACHE..."
            rm -rf "$CACHE"
            mkdir -p "$CACHE"
            mv "$SRC" "$CACHE/"
          fi
        fi

        # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
        # shared workspace (bench leftovers held by docker containers) —
        # log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
        if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
        fi
        if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
          if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
          fi
        fi
        mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

        CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a live
          # bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build the
          # checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A bench
          # leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path; if one
          # ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 "$REPO_URL" "$CLONE_TARGET"
        if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
          while IFS= read -r entry; do
            name="$(basename "$entry")"
            if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then

      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # gh-1600 AC2: hardened mirror-checkout — the bare `rm -rf
      # "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` used to fail the whole checkout on stale
