{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1600 `[daily-publish] testflight leg failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: the `daily-publish` testflight leg failed through two independent
layers — (L1-routing) the iOS jobs routed onto the Linux self-hosted runner,
and (L1-isolation) the shared self-hosted workspace was polluted by bench
leftovers that broke the mirror-checkout.

**Root cause**:

1. **Routing** — `build-mobile.yml` jobs `build-ios` (line 605) and
   `submit-ios` (line 1032), plus `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (line 92),
   pinned the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`.
   That list also matches the labels advertised by the repo's Linux
   self-hosted box, so `Build iOS IPA` executed on Linux (`/home/runner/…`)
   with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode → `bundle: command not found` → `exit 127` at
   *Install fastlane* (run 38516656653); the 2026-10-15 night run
   additionally died on `security: command not found`. Same routing-bug
   class gh-1005 solved for `ci.yml` with the unique `macos-m5` label.
2. **Workspace isolation** — `bench-harbor.yml` wrote its harbor output
   INSIDE the build workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`,
   trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers). On the persistent
   self-hosted box the mobile legs' checkout ran a bare
   `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"`, which failed on the docker-held leftovers
   (`rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1) and failed the checkout before any
   build step.

**Impact**: every scheduled `daily-publish` TestFlight leg fails — no iOS
build ships; a bench run immediately followed by a mobile build on the same
box also breaks the checkout even when routing is fixed.

**Fix approach** (minimal, per the ticket's F-A/F-B; F-C is #1262's scope):

- **F-A**: pin all three macOS publish-leg jobs to
  `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique registration label of
  fa-m5-1, the repo's ONE self-hosted macOS runner (the exact convention
  ci.yml's `cube-kernel-live` already uses since gh-1005).
- **F-B (producer)**: bench-harbor writes its output to
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace
  path); the artifact + Harbor Hub uploads follow; a new `always()` step
  tears the shard's docker containers down BEFORE removing the output dir
  (both best-effort so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict).
- **F-B (consumer)**: all three mirror-checkout jobs (`build-ios`,
  `submit-ios`, `build-macos`) get the hardened clean INLINE — log-and-prune
  (removable paths removed; a still-blocked remainder moved aside into
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-workspace-*`; a surviving mount stub cloned around) —
  so a stale unremovable path can never fail the checkout. build-macos keeps
  its per-arch build cache park/restore, now best-effort (a lost cache
  rebuilds from scratch, never fails the checkout).
- **Why INLINE, not a composite action**: round 1 of this leg (WIP
  `ede8c5f3`) factored the checkout into
  `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` and consumed it via
  `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout`. That is incorrect on these
  runners: a local `./` action resolves against `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` AT STEP
  TIME, and on the persistent box that workspace is the PREVIOUS run's tree
  (or nothing) — the action file would be MISSING on the first post-merge
  run and silently STALE afterwards, because the checkout step is exactly
  the thing that materializes the tree. The inline scripts always execute
  the committed copy of the commit under test. (The action also assigned
  its `preserve-cache-dir` input single-quoted, keeping the caller's
  `$HOME` token literal — the cache would have parked in a junk
  `./'$HOME'/…` dir; the inline script's `BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/…"`
  expands natively.) The composite action is deleted.

**Previous attempt**: none merged — this is the first fix landed for
gh-1600 (a prior dev run 38733592508 saved WIP `ede8c5f3` but never
concluded; this round verified the WIP's intent, corrected its composite
action design, and completed verification).

## Verification

- RED: on `origin/main` the shape the regression test asserts is absent —
  `build-mobile.yml:605/1032` + `build-macos.yml:92` carry the generic
  `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` labels, `bench-harbor.yml:602/610` write
  `-o jobs` into the workspace, and no hardened clean exists — the
  reproduction test fails on base.
- GREEN: `dart test test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — 10 tests
  pass (AC1 runner-pin asserts + AC2 isolation asserts, incl. the audit
  that NO self-hosted job in either leg skips the `macos-m5` pin, the
  no-local-action assert, and the cache-park-before-clean assert).
- Behavioral sim of the REAL committed scripts (extracted from the workflow
  YAML and executed in a sandbox with a fake local mirror), 3 modes: clean
  clone; build-macos cache parked under the expanded `$HOME` + restored
  (with no junk literal-`$HOME` dir); surviving-stub clone-around with the
  remainder moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP` — all pass. Embedded scripts pass
  `bash -n`; all touched YAML parses.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (fresh run against the
  final tree — see response.md for the final count).

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1600 `[daily-publish] testflight leg failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: the `daily-publish` testflight leg failed twice over two independent
layers — (L1-routing) the iOS jobs routed onto the Linux self-hosted runner
and (L1-isolation) the shared self-hosted workspace was polluted by bench
leftovers that broke the mirror-checkout.

**Root cause**:

1. **Routing** — `build-mobile.yml` jobs `build-ios` (line 605) and
   `submit-ios` (line 1032), plus `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (line 92),
   pinned the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`.
   That list also matches the labels advertised by the repo's Linux
   self-hosted box, so `Build iOS IPA` executed on Linux (`/home/runner/…`)
   with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode → `bundle: command not found` → `exit 127` at
   *Install fastlane* (run 38516656653); the 2026-10-15 night run
   additionally died on `security: command not found`. Same routing bug
   class gh-1005 solved for `ci.yml` with the unique `macos-m5` label.
2. **Workspace isolation** — `bench-harbor.yml` wrote its harbor output
   INSIDE the build workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`,
   trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers). On the persistent
   self-hosted box the mobile legs' checkout ran a bare
   `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"`, which failed on the docker-held leftovers
   (`rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1) and failed the checkout before any
   build step.

**Impact**: every scheduled `daily-publish` TestFlight leg fails — no iOS
build ships; a bench run immediately followed by a mobile build on the same
box also breaks the checkout even when routing is fixed.

**Fix approach** (minimal, per the ticket's F-A/F-B; F-C is #1262's scope):

- **F-A**: pin all three macOS publish-leg jobs to
  `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique registration label of
  fa-m5-1, the repo's ONE self-hosted macOS runner (the exact convention
  ci.yml's `cube-kernel-live` already uses since gh-1005).
- **F-B (producer)**: bench-harbor writes its output to
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace
  path); the artifact + Harbor Hub uploads follow; a new `always()` step
  tears the shard's docker containers down BEFORE removing the output dir
  (both best-effort so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict).
- **F-B (consumer)**: the three mirror-checkout jobs share a hardened
  composite action `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` — the workspace clean
  is log-and-prune (removable paths removed, a still-blocked remainder
  moved aside into `$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-workspace-*`, a surviving mount
  stub cloned around) so a stale unremovable path can never fail the
  checkout; build-macos's per-arch build cache is preserved via
  `preserve-path`/`preserve-cache-dir` (a literal `$HOME` token in the
  cache dir is expanded at run time — GH expressions cannot see the
  runner's HOME).

**Previous attempt**: none merged — this is the first fix landed for
gh-1600 (a prior dev run 38733592508 saved WIP `ede8c5f3` but never
concluded; this round verified/extended that WIP).

## Verification

- RED: on `origin/main` the shape the regression test asserts is absent —
  `build-mobile.yml:605/1032` + `build-macos.yml:92` carry the generic
  `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` labels, `bench-harbor.yml:602/610` write
  `-o jobs` into the workspace, and `.github/actions/mirror-checkout/`
  does not exist — the reproduction test fails on base.
- GREEN: `dart test test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — 10 tests
  pass (AC1 runner-pin asserts + AC2 isolation asserts, incl. the audit
  that NO self-hosted job in either leg skips the `macos-m5` pin).
- Behavioral sim of the composite action's script (3 modes): clean clone,
  per-arch cache parked under the EXPANDED `$HOME` + restored (catches the
  literal-`$HOME` assignment bug), surviving-stub clone-around with the
  remainder moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP` — all pass; embedded scripts pass
  `bash -n`; all touched YAML parses.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (see response.md for
  the final count).

messages.preview: **Design flaw found in the WIP**: `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` resolves the action from `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` **at step time** — but these jobs never run `actions/checkout`; the composite a…

blocks.text:
build-ios looks right. One consideration: `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` — a local composite action requires the action to exist in the checked-out tree... but the checkout happens VIA the action (chicken-and-egg!). On GitHub Actions, `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` resolves the action from the workspace — the runner needs the repo files at that point. In the ORIGINAL flow, the checkout was a `run:` step that cloned into `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` manually — the workspace at step time was the (nearly) empty shared dir, NOT a Actions-checkout-populated tree.

CRITICAL: how does `uses: ./.github/actions/...` behave when the workspace has NOT been checked out by actions/checkout yet? GitHub's composite action resolution reads `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/actions/mirror-checkout` — if the workspace is empty (the persistent-box scenario), the action file DOESN'T EXIST → the step fails with "Can't find 'action.yml'".

Wait — but is that true? For `uses: ./path` local actions in a workflow, the runner resolves the path relative to `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` AT STEP EXECUTION TIME. GitHub docs: "Path to the directory containing the action, relative to the repository's root" — for jobs that don't run actions/checkout first, a local action can't be used (docs say local actions only run after checkout in the SAME job... actually the requirement is the files exist in the workspace).

Hmm, but the runner DOES NOT auto-materialize the repo. actions/checkout materializes it. In build-ios, the first step updates the mirror (run step), second step is the composite action — at that point the workspace on the persistent runner is... whatever the PREVIOUS run left there! Because these jobs deliberately do NOT use actions/checkout — they hand-clone via mirror. On a hosted runner the workspace starts empty → `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` would FAIL (no such file).

On the shared self-hosted runner, the workspace holds the previous run's checkout (the previous workflow that ran there — could be ANY workflow, e.g. an old commit of the repo that may pre-date the action). So:
- If the previous state of the workspace has a repo at some ref BEFORE this change lands → the action file doesn't exist there → the step fails → the leg stays red! Self-hosted persistent workspaces make this fragile: `uses: ./local/action` reads the WORKSPACE copy, which is the LAST-RUN's tree, not this commit's tree.

Wait, actually — for local composite actions, does the runner use the workspace file, or does it download the workflow-ref version? For `uses: ./.github/actions/x` in a workflow triggered on a ref, the runner resolves the local path from the workspace, yes. GitHub docs state local actions require a checkout step first ("When a workflow uses local actions, the action must be checked out before the step that uses it"). Since these jobs replaced actions/checkout with a MIRROR clone step that runs AFTER... no — the mirror-clone WAS the checkout step; now it's INSIDE the composite action. So at composite-action resolution time the workspace has NO fresh tree.

Hmm, but on this PERSISTENT runner the workspace is shared and typically holds the PREVIOUS run's checkout (of whatever branch/workflow ran last there — build-macos ran from a release tag, bench didn't touch the workspace anymore after our fix...). If the leftover tree is from a commit that predates `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (i.e., everything before this fix merges), the FIRST run after merge fails: "Can't find 'action.yml'". Subsequent runs would find the action (from whatever previous run left), which may STILL be a stale version of the action — the composite action would silently be a stale copy, never the commit-under-test's version!

This is a real design flaw in the WIP. The composite action approach only works if the workspace reliably contains the current commit's action file BEFORE the step runs. It doesn't — the checkout IS the step.

How do other workflows in this repo handle self-hosted mirror checkout? ci.yml's cube-kernel-live uses `actions/checkout` (hosted pattern — the runner downloads the tarball; `uses:` local actions after actions/checkout is fine). For build-macos/build-mobile on the persistent box, the whole point of the mirror-checkout `run:` step was to avoid the slow full checkout.

Options:
A. Revert to inline `run:` steps (no composite action) with the hardened logic inlined in each of the three jobs. Duplicates the script 3×, but each job executes exactly its committed copy. The test can still assert shape (e.g. all three carry the log-and-prune lines).
B. Bootstrap step: a tiny `run:` step that fetches JUST `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` from the mirror (git archive / sparse clone) into the workspace BEFORE `uses:`. E.g. `git -C $MIRROR archive <sha> .github/actions/mirror-checkout | tar -x -C $GITHUB_WORKSPACE`? But which sha? `github.sha` — the mirror was just updated (fetch origin) so `github.sha` exists in it. That's doable but adds a step with its own failure modes; and `git archive` from a bare mirror with `--depth=1` clone... the mirror is a full --mirror clone, fine.
C. Put the script in `scripts/` (committed file) and have each job's `run:` step call it after the mirror-clone bootstraps the script the same way... same resolution problem — the script must exist in the workspace before the checkout.

Honestly, option A (inline in each job) is the pragmatic, standard approach for these mirror-checkout steps and eliminates the resolution hazard entirely. But it loses the single-source-of-truth. The repo values: "Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things" — the established way for these three jobs was an inline `run:` checkout script. The composite action was the previous round's invention and it's BROKEN for the first run after landing (and stale-version runs after).

Actually wait — let me reconsider. On the FIRST run after the fix lands: what's in the persistent workspace? The previous run's checkout. What ran before on fa-m5-1? cube-kernel-live (ci.yml, uses actions/checkout → workspace = ci run's tree at whatever sha CI ran), release/build-macos legs (mirror-clone at release shas). For a merged fix at sha S, the first build-mobile run's workspace contains an OLDER tree (pre-action). `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` → the runner looks for `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/actions/mirror-checkout/action.yml` → absent → job FAILS at the checkout step → TestFlight leg STILL RED. The fix would never bootstrap itself. And even later, the action file in the workspace is whatever the last successful run of ANY workflow left — potentially months stale.

So the composite action MUST be fed the current tree somehow, or inlined. Let me check how the previous round's test asserts things and restructure:

- Each of the three jobs' checkout `run:` scripts must contain the log-and-prune lines (`rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true`, `stale-workspace`, `git clone --reference`).

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1600 `[daily-publish] testflight leg failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: the `daily-publish` testflight leg failed through two independent
layers — (L1-routing) the iOS jobs routed onto the Linux self-hosted runner,
and (L1-isolation) the shared self-hosted workspace was polluted by bench
leftovers that broke the mirror-checkout.

**Root cause**:

1. **Routing** — `build-mobile.yml` jobs `build-ios` (line 605) and
   `submit-ios` (line 1032), plus `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (line 92),
   pinned the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`.
   That list also matches the labels advertised by the repo's Linux
   self-hosted box, so `Build iOS IPA` executed on Linux (`/home/runner/…`)
   with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode → `bundle: command not found` → `exit 127` at
   *Install fastlane* (run 38516656653); the 2026-10-15 night run
   additionally died on `security: command not found`. Same routing-bug
   class gh-1005 solved for `ci.yml` with the unique `macos-m5` label.
2. **Workspace isolation** — `bench-harbor.yml` wrote its harbor output
   INSIDE the build workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`,
   trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers). On the persistent
   self-hosted box the mobile legs' checkout ran a bare
   `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"`, which failed on the docker-held leftovers
   (`rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1) and failed the checkout before any
   build step.

**Impact**: every scheduled `daily-publish` TestFlight leg fails — no iOS
build ships; a bench run immediately followed by a mobile build on the same
box also breaks the checkout even when routing is fixed.

**Fix approach** (minimal, per the ticket's F-A/F-B; F-C is #1262's scope):

- **F-A**: pin all three macOS publish-leg jobs to
  `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique registration label of
  fa-m5-1, the repo's ONE self-hosted macOS runner (the exact convention
  ci.yml's `cube-kernel-live` already uses since gh-1005).
- **F-B (producer)**: bench-harbor writes its output to
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace
  path); the artifact + Harbor Hub uploads follow; a new `always()` step
  tears the shard's docker containers down BEFORE removing the output dir
  (both best-effort so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict).
- **F-B (consumer)**: all three mirror-checkout jobs (`build-ios`,
  `submit-ios`, `build-macos`) get the hardened clean INLINE — log-and-prune
  (removable paths removed; a still-blocked remainder moved aside into
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-workspace-*`; a surviving mount stub cloned around) —
  so a stale unremovable path can never fail the checkout. build-macos keeps
  its per-arch build cache park/restore, now best-effort (a lost cache
  rebuilds from scratch, never fails the checkout).
- **Why INLINE, not a composite action**: round 1 of this leg (WIP
  `ede8c5f3`) factored the checkout into
  `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` and consumed it via
  `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout`. That is incorrect on these
  runners: a local `./` action resolves against `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` AT STEP
  TIME, and on the persistent box that workspace is the PREVIOUS run's tree
  (or nothing) — the action file would be MISSING on the first post-merge
  run and silently STALE afterwards, because the checkout step is exactly
  the thing that materializes the tree. The inline scripts always execute
  the committed copy of the commit under test. (The action also assigned
  its `preserve-cache-dir` input single-quoted, keeping the caller's
  `$HOME` token literal — the cache would have parked in a junk
  `./'$HOME'/…` dir; the inline script's `BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/…"`
  expands natively.) The composite action is deleted.

**Previous attempt**: none merged — this is the first fix landed for
gh-1600 (a prior dev run 38733592508 saved WIP `ede8c5f3` but never
concluded; this round verified the WIP's intent, corrected its composite
action design, and completed verification).

## Verification

- RED: on `origin/main` the shape the regression test asserts is absent —
  `build-mobile.yml:605/1032` + `build-macos.yml:92` carry the generic
  `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` labels, `bench-harbor.yml:602/610` write
  `-o jobs` into the workspace, and no hardened clean exists — the
  reproduction test fails on base.
- GREEN: `dart test test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — 10 tests
  pass (AC1 runner-pin asserts + AC2 isolation asserts, incl. the audit
  that NO self-hosted job in either leg skips the `macos-m5` pin, the
  no-local-action assert, and the cache-park-before-clean assert).
- Behavioral sim of the REAL committed scripts (extracted from the workflow
  YAML and executed in a sandbox with a fake local mirror), 3 modes: clean
  clone; build-macos cache parked under the expanded `$HOME` + restored
  (with no junk literal-`$HOME` dir); surviving-stub clone-around with the
  remainder moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP` — all pass. Embedded scripts pass
  `bash -n`; all touched YAML parses.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (fresh run against the
  final tree — see response.md for the final count).

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1600 `[daily-publish] testflight leg failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: the `daily-publish` testflight leg failed twice over two independent
layers — (L1-routing) the iOS jobs routed onto the Linux self-hosted runner
and (L1-isolation) the shared self-hosted workspace was polluted by bench
leftovers that broke the mirror-checkout.

**Root cause**:

1. **Routing** — `build-mobile.yml` jobs `build-ios` (line 605) and
   `submit-ios` (line 1032), plus `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (line 92),
   pinned the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`.
   That list also matches the labels advertised by the repo's Linux
   self-hosted box, so `Build iOS IPA` executed on Linux (`/home/runner/…`)
   with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode → `bundle: command not found` → `exit 127` at
   *Install fastlane* (run 38516656653); the 2026-10-15 night run
   additionally died on `security: command not found`. Same routing bug
   class gh-1005 solved for `ci.yml` with the unique `macos-m5` label.
2. **Workspace isolation** — `bench-harbor.yml` wrote its harbor output
   INSIDE the build workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`,
   trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers). On the persistent
   self-hosted box the mobile legs' checkout ran a bare
   `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"`, which failed on the docker-held leftovers
   (`rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1) and failed the checkout before any
   build step.

**Impact**: every scheduled `daily-publish` TestFlight leg fails — no iOS
build ships; a bench run immediately followed by a mobile build on the same
box also breaks the checkout even when routing is fixed.

**Fix approach** (minimal, per the ticket's F-A/F-B; F-C is #1262's scope):

- **F-A**: pin all three macOS publish-leg jobs to
  `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique registration label of
  fa-m5-1, the repo's ONE self-hosted macOS runner (the exact convention
  ci.yml's `cube-kernel-live` already uses since gh-1005).
- **F-B (producer)**: bench-harbor writes its output to
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace
  path); the artifact + Harbor Hub uploads follow; a new `always()` step
  tears the shard's docker containers down BEFORE removing the output dir
  (both best-effort so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict).
- **F-B (consumer)**: the three mirror-checkout jobs share a hardened
  composite action `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` — the workspace clean
  is log-and-prune (removable paths removed, a still-blocked remainder
  moved aside into `$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-workspace-*`, a surviving mount
  stub cloned around) so a stale unremovable path can never fail the
  checkout; build-macos's per-arch build cache is preserved via
  `preserve-path`/`preserve-cache-dir` (a literal `$HOME` token in the
  cache dir is expanded at run time — GH expressions cannot see the
  runner's HOME).

**Previous attempt**: none merged — this is the first fix landed for
gh-1600 (a prior dev run 38733592508 saved WIP `ede8c5f3` but never
concluded; this round verified/extended that WIP).

## Verification

- RED: on `origin/main` the shape the regression test asserts is absent —
  `build-mobile.yml:605/1032` + `build-macos.yml:92` carry the generic
  `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` labels, `bench-harbor.yml:602/610` write
  `-o jobs` into the workspace, and `.github/actions/mirror-checkout/`
  does not exist — the reproduction test fails on base.
- GREEN: `dart test test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — 10 tests
  pass (AC1 runner-pin asserts + AC2 isolation asserts, incl. the audit
  that NO self-hosted job in either leg skips the `macos-m5` pin).
- Behavioral sim of the composite action's script (3 modes): clean clone,
  per-arch cache parked under the EXPANDED `$HOME` + restored (catches the
  literal-`$HOME` assignment bug), surviving-stub clone-around with the
  remainder moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP` — all pass; embedded scripts pass
  `bash -n`; all touched YAML parses.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (see response.md for
  the final count).

build-ios looks right. One consideration: `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` — a local composite action requires the action to exist in the checked-out tree... but the checkout happens VIA the action (chicken-and-egg!). On GitHub Actions, `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` resolves the action from the workspace — the runner needs the repo files at that point. In the ORIGINAL flow, the checkout was a `run:` step that cloned into `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` manually — the workspace at step time was the (nearly) empty shared dir, NOT a Actions-checkout-populated tree.

CRITICAL: how does `uses: ./.github/actions/...` behave when the workspace has NOT been checked out by actions/checkout yet? GitHub's composite action resolution reads `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/actions/mirror-checkout` — if the workspace is empty (the persistent-box scenario), the action file DOESN'T EXIST → the step fails with "Can't find 'action.yml'".

Wait — but is that true? For `uses: ./path` local actions in a workflow, the runner resolves the path relative to `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` AT STEP EXECUTION TIME. GitHub docs: "Path to the directory containing the action, relative to the repository's root" — for jobs that don't run actions/checkout first, a local action can't be used (docs say local actions only run after checkout in the SAME job... actually the requirement is the files exist in the workspace).

Hmm, but the runner DOES NOT auto-materialize the repo. actions/checkout materializes it. In build-ios, the first step updates the mirror (run step), second step is the composite action — at that point the workspace on the persistent runner is... whatever the PREVIOUS run left there! Because these jobs deliberately do NOT use actions/checkout — they hand-clone via mirror. On a hosted runner the workspace starts empty → `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` would FAIL (no such file).

On the shared self-hosted runner, the workspace holds the previous run's checkout (the previous workflow that ran there — could be ANY workflow, e.g. an old commit of the repo that may pre-date the action). So:
- If the previous state of the workspace has a repo at some ref BEFORE this change lands → the action file doesn't exist there → the step fails → the leg stays red! Self-hosted persistent workspaces make this fragile: `uses: ./local/action` reads the WORKSPACE copy, which is the LAST-RUN's tree, not this commit's tree.

Wait, actually — for local composite actions, does the runner use the workspace file, or does it download the workflow-ref version? For `uses: ./.github/actions/x` in a workflow triggered on a ref, the runner resolves the local path from the workspace, yes. GitHub docs state local actions require a checkout step first ("When a workflow uses local actions, the action must be checked out before the step that uses it"). Since these jobs replaced actions/checkout with a MIRROR clone step that runs AFTER... no — the mirror-clone WAS the checkout step; now it's INSIDE the composite action. So at composite-action resolution time the workspace has NO fresh tree.

Hmm, but on this PERSISTENT runner the workspace is shared and typically holds the PREVIOUS run's checkout (of whatever branch/workflow ran last there — build-macos ran from a release tag, bench didn't touch the workspace anymore after our fix...). If the leftover tree is from a commit that predates `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (i.e., everything before this fix merges), the FIRST run after merge fails: "Can't find 'action.yml'". Subsequent runs would find the action (from whatever previous run left), which may STILL be a stale version of the action — the composite action would silently be a stale copy, never the commit-under-test's version!

This is a real design flaw in the WIP. The composite action approach only works if the workspace reliably contains the current commit's action file BEFORE the step runs. It doesn't — the checkout IS the step.

How do other workflows in this repo handle self-hosted mirror checkout? ci.yml's cube-kernel-live uses `actions/checkout` (hosted pattern — the runner downloads the tarball; `uses:` local actions after actions/checkout is fine). For build-macos/build-mobile on the persistent box, the whole point of the mirror-checkout `run:` step was to avoid the slow full checkout.

A. Revert to inline `run:` steps (no composite action) with the hardened logic inlined in each of the three jobs. Duplicates the script 3×, but each job executes exactly its committed copy. The test can still assert shape (e.g. all three carry the log-and-prune lines).

E.g. `git -C $MIRROR archive <sha> .github/actions/mirror-checkout | tar -x -C $GITHUB_WORKSPACE`? But which sha? `github.sha` — the mirror was just updated (fetch origin) so `github.sha` exists in it. That's doable but adds a step with its own failure modes; and `git archive` from a bare mirror with `--depth=1` clone... the mirror is a full --mirror clone, fine.
C. Put the script in `scripts/` (committed file) and have each job's `run:` step call it after the mirror-clone bootstraps the script the same way... same resolution problem — the script must exist in the workspace before the checkout.

Honestly, option A (inline in each job) is the pragmatic, standard approach for these mirror-checkout steps and eliminates the resolution hazard entirely. But it loses the single-source-of-truth. The repo values: "Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things" — the established way for these three jobs was an inline `run:` checkout script. {"content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1600 `[daily-publish] testflight leg failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: the `daily-publish` testflight leg failed through two independent
layers — (L1-routing) the iOS jobs routed onto the Linux self-hosted runner,
and (L1-isolation) the shared self-hosted workspace was polluted by bench
leftovers that broke the mirror-checkout.

**Root cause**:

1. **Routing** — `build-mobile.yml` jobs `build-ios` (line 605) and
   `submit-ios` (line 1032), plus `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (line 92),
   pinned the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`.
   That list also matches the labels advertised by the repo's Linux
   self-hosted box, so `Build iOS IPA` executed on Linux (`/home/runner/…`)
   with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode → `bundle: command not found` → `exit 127` at
   *Install fastlane* (run 38516656653); the 2026-10-15 night run
   additionally died on `security: command not found`. Same routing-bug
   class gh-1005 solved for `ci.yml` with the unique `macos-m5` label.
2. **Workspace isolation** — `bench-harbor.yml` wrote its harbor output
   INSIDE the build workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`,
   trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers). On the persistent
   self-hosted box the mobile legs' checkout ran a bare
   `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"`, which failed on the docker-held leftovers
   (`rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1) and failed the checkout before any
   build step.

**Impact**: every scheduled `daily-publish` TestFlight leg fails — no iOS
build ships; a bench run immediately followed by a mobile build on the same
box also breaks the checkout even when routing is fixed.

**Fix approach** (minimal, per the ticket's F-A/F-B; F-C is #1262's scope):

- **F-A**: pin all three macOS publish-leg jobs to
  `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique registration label of
  fa-m5-1, the repo's ONE self-hosted macOS runner (the exact convention
  ci.yml's `cube-kernel-live` already uses since gh-1005).
- **F-B (producer)**: bench-harbor writes its output to
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace
  path); the artifact + Harbor Hub uploads follow; a new `always()` step
  tears the shard's docker containers down BEFORE removing the output dir
  (both best-effort so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict).
- **F-B (consumer)**: all three mirror-checkout jobs (`build-ios`,
  `submit-ios`, `build-macos`) get the hardened clean INLINE — log-and-prune
  (removable paths removed; a still-blocked remainder moved aside into
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-workspace-*`; a surviving mount stub cloned around) —
  so a stale unremovable path can never fail the checkout. build-macos keeps
  its per-arch build cache park/restore, now best-effort (a lost cache
  rebuilds from scratch, never fails the checkout).
- **Why INLINE, not a composite action**: round 1 of this leg (WIP
  `ede8c5f3`) factored the checkout into
  `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` and consumed it via
  `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout`. That is incorrect on these
  runners: a local `./` action resolves against `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` AT STEP
  TIME, and on the persistent box that workspace is the PREVIOUS run's tree
  (or nothing) — the action file would be MISSING on the first post-merge
  run and silently STALE afterwards, because the checkout step is exactly
  the thing that materializes the tree. The inline scripts always execute
  the committed copy of the commit under test. (The action also assigned
  its `preserve-cache-dir` input single-quoted, keeping the caller's
  `$HOME` token literal — the cache would have parked in a junk
  `./'$HOME'/…` dir; the inline script's `BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/…"`
  expands natively.) The composite action is deleted.

**Previous attempt**: none merged — this is the first fix landed for
gh-1600 (a prior dev run 38733592508 saved WIP `ede8c5f3` but never
concluded; this round verified the WIP's intent, corrected its composite
action design, and completed verification).

- RED: on `origin/main` the shape the regression test asserts is absent —

  that NO self-hosted job in either leg skips the `macos-m5` pin, the
  no-local-action assert, and the cache-park-before-clean assert).

  remainder moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP` — all pass. Embedded scripts pass
  `bash -n`; all touched YAML parses.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (fresh run against the
  final tree — see response.md for the final count).

GitHub's composite action resolution reads `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/actions/mirror-checkout` — if the workspace is empty (the persistent-box scenario), the action file DOESN'T EXIST → the step fails with "Can't find 'action.yml'".

Wait — but is that true? For `uses: ./path` local actions in a workflow, the runner resolves the path relative to `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` AT STEP EXECUTION TIME. GitHub docs: "Path to the directory containing the action, relative to the repository's root" — for jobs that don't run actions/checkout first, a local action can't be used (docs say local actions only run after checkout in the SAME job... actually the requirement is the files exist in the workspace).

Hmm, but the runner DOES NOT auto-materialize the repo. actions/checkout materializes it. In build-ios, the first step updates the mirror (run step), second step is the composite action — at that point the workspace on the persistent runner is... whatever the PREVIOUS run left there! Because these jobs deliberately do NOT use actions/checkout — they hand-clone via mirror. On a hosted runner the workspace starts empty → `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` would FAIL (no such file).

On the shared self-hosted runner, the workspace holds the previous run's checkout (the previous workflow that ran there — could be ANY workflow, e.g. an old commit of the repo that may pre-date the action). So:

For `uses: ./.github/actions/x` in a workflow triggered on a ref, the runner resolves the local path from the workspace, yes. Hmm, but on this PERSISTENT runner the workspace is shared and typically holds the PREVIOUS run's checkout (of whatever branch/workflow ran last there — build-macos ran from a release tag, bench didn't touch the workspace anymore after our fix...). Subsequent runs would find the action (from whatever previous run left), which may STILL be a stale version of the action — the composite action would silently be a stale copy, never the commit-under-test's version!

This is a real design flaw in the WIP. The composite action approach only works if the workspace reliably contains the current commit's action file BEFORE the step runs. It doesn't — the checkout IS the step.

How do other workflows in this repo handle self-hosted mirror checkout? ci.yml's cube-kernel-live uses `actions/checkout` (hosted pattern — the runner downloads the tarball; `uses:` local actions after actions/checkout is fine).       # gh-1600 AC2: hardened mirror-checkout — the bare `rm -rf

      # unremovable leftovers in the persistent shared workspace (bench
      # docker leftovers, jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/). Log-and-prune clean +
      # clone-around-stub; the per-arch build cache is parked outside the
      # workspace before the clean and restored after the clone (best-effort:
      # a lost cache re-builds from scratch, it never fails the checkout).
      # INLINE (not a composite action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...`
      # actions resolve against $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time — on this box
      # that is the PREVIOUS run's tree, and this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          MAIN_MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-$ARCH"

          echo "HOME=$HOME"
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MAIN_MIRROR=$MAIN_MIRROR"
          echo "ARCH=$ARCH"

          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mkdir -p "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/" \
              || echo "::warning::could not park the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi

          cd /tmp

          # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
          # shared workspace — log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MAIN_MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          if [ -d "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" ]; then
            echo "Restoring macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf build/macos 2>/dev/null || true
            mkdir -p build
            mv "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" build/ \
              || echo "::warning::could not restore the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi","oldText":"      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

      # docker leftovers, jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/). The per-arch build
      # cache below is parked outside the workspace before the clean and
      # restored after the clone (preserve-path/preserve-cache-dir).
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors

        with:

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1600 `[daily-publish] testflight leg failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: the `daily-publish` testflight leg failed through two independent
layers — (L1-routing) the iOS jobs routed onto the Linux self-hosted runner,
and (L1-isolation) the shared self-hosted workspace was polluted by bench
leftovers that broke the mirror-checkout.

**Root cause**:

1. **Routing** — `build-mobile.yml` jobs `build-ios` (line 605) and
   `submit-ios` (line 1032), plus `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (line 92),
   pinned the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`.
   That list also matches the labels advertised by the repo's Linux
   self-hosted box, so `Build iOS IPA` executed on Linux (`/home/runner/…`)
   with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode → `bundle: command not found` → `exit 127` at
   *Install fastlane* (run 38516656653); the 2026-10-15 night run
   additionally died on `security: command not found`. Same routing-bug
   class gh-1005 solved for `ci.yml` with the unique `macos-m5` label.
2. **Workspace isolation** — `bench-harbor.yml` wrote its harbor output
   INSIDE the build workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`,
   trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers). On the persistent
   self-hosted box the mobile legs' checkout ran a bare
   `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"`, which failed on the docker-held leftovers
   (`rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1) and failed the checkout before any
   build step.

**Impact**: every scheduled `daily-publish` TestFlight leg fails — no iOS
build ships; a bench run immediately followed by a mobile build on the same
box also breaks the checkout even when routing is fixed.

**Fix approach** (minimal, per the ticket's F-A/F-B; F-C is #1262's scope):

- **F-A**: pin all three macOS publish-leg jobs to
  `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique registration label of
  fa-m5-1, the repo's ONE self-hosted macOS runner (the exact convention
  ci.yml's `cube-kernel-live` already uses since gh-1005).
- **F-B (producer)**: bench-harbor writes its output to
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace
  path); the artifact + Harbor Hub uploads follow; a new `always()` step
  tears the shard's docker containers down BEFORE removing the output dir
  (both best-effort so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict).
- **F-B (consumer)**: all three mirror-checkout jobs (`build-ios`,
  `submit-ios`, `build-macos`) get the hardened clean INLINE — log-and-prune
  (removable paths removed; a still-blocked remainder moved aside into
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-workspace-*`; a surviving mount stub cloned around) —
  so a stale unremovable path can never fail the checkout. build-macos keeps
  its per-arch build cache park/restore, now best-effort (a lost cache
  rebuilds from scratch, never fails the checkout).
- **Why INLINE, not a composite action**: round 1 of this leg (WIP
  `ede8c5f3`) factored the checkout into
  `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` and consumed it via
  `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout`. That is incorrect on these
  runners: a local `./` action resolves against `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` AT STEP
  TIME, and on the persistent box that workspace is the PREVIOUS run's tree
  (or nothing) — the action file would be MISSING on the first post-merge
  run and silently STALE afterwards, because the checkout step is exactly
  the thing that materializes the tree. The inline scripts always execute
  the committed copy of the commit under test. (The action also assigned
  its `preserve-cache-dir` input single-quoted, keeping the caller's
  `$HOME` token literal — the cache would have parked in a junk
  `./'$HOME'/…` dir; the inline script's `BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/…"`
  expands natively.) The composite action is deleted.

**Previous attempt**: none merged — this is the first fix landed for
gh-1600 (a prior dev run 38733592508 saved WIP `ede8c5f3` but never
concluded; this round verified the WIP's intent, corrected its composite
action design, and completed verification).

## Verification

- RED: on `origin/main` the shape the regression test asserts is absent —
  `build-mobile.yml:605/1032` + `build-macos.yml:92` carry the generic
  `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` labels, `bench-harbor.yml:602/610` write
  `-o jobs` into the workspace, and no hardened clean exists — the
  reproduction test fails on base.
- GREEN: `dart test test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — 10 tests
  pass (AC1 runner-pin asserts + AC2 isolation asserts, incl. the audit
  that NO self-hosted job in either leg skips the `macos-m5` pin, the
  no-local-action assert, and the cache-park-before-clean assert).
- Behavioral sim of the REAL committed scripts (extracted from the workflow
  YAML and executed in a sandbox with a fake local mirror), 3 modes: clean
  clone; build-macos cache parked under the expanded `$HOME` + restored
  (with no junk literal-`$HOME` dir); surviving-stub clone-around with the
  remainder moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP` — all pass. Embedded scripts pass
  `bash -n`; all touched YAML parses.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (fresh run against the
  final tree — see response.md for the final count).

GitHub's composite action resolution reads `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/actions/mirror-checkout` — if the workspace is empty (the persistent-box scenario), the action file DOESN'T EXIST → the step fails with "Can't find 'action.yml'".

GitHub docs: "Path to the directory containing the action, relative to the repository's root" — for jobs that don't run actions/checkout first, a local action can't be used (docs say local actions only run after checkout in the SAME job... actually the requirement is the files exist in the workspace).

Hmm, but the runner DOES NOT auto-materialize the repo. actions/checkout materializes it. In build-ios, the first step updates the mirror (run step), second step is the composite action — at that point the workspace on the persistent runner is... whatever the PREVIOUS run left there! Because these jobs deliberately do NOT use actions/checkout — they hand-clone via mirror. On a hosted runner the workspace starts empty → `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` would FAIL (no such file).

On the shared self-hosted runner, the workspace holds the previous run's checkout (the previous workflow that ran there — could be ANY workflow, e.g. an old commit of the repo that may pre-date the action). So:

GitHub docs state local actions require a checkout step first ("When a workflow uses local actions, the action must be checked out before the step that uses it"). Hmm, but on this PERSISTENT runner the workspace is shared and typically holds the PREVIOUS run's checkout (of whatever branch/workflow ran last there — build-macos ran from a release tag, bench didn't touch the workspace anymore after our fix...). If the leftover tree is from a commit that predates `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (i.e., everything before this fix merges), the FIRST run after merge fails: "Can't find 'action.yml'". Subsequent runs would find the action (from whatever previous run left), which may STILL be a stale version of the action — the composite action would silently be a stale copy, never the commit-under-test's version!

This is a real design flaw in the WIP. The composite action approach only works if the workspace reliably contains the current commit's action file BEFORE the step runs. It doesn't — the checkout IS the step.

How do other workflows in this repo handle self-hosted mirror checkout? ci.yml's cube-kernel-live uses `actions/checkout` (hosted pattern — the runner downloads the tarball; `uses:` local actions after actions/checkout is fine). {"content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1600 `[daily-publish] testflight leg failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: the `daily-publish` testflight leg failed through two independent
layers — (L1-routing) the iOS jobs routed onto the Linux self-hosted runner,
and (L1-isolation) the shared self-hosted workspace was polluted by bench
leftovers that broke the mirror-checkout.

**Root cause**:

1. **Routing** — `build-mobile.yml` jobs `build-ios` (line 605) and
   `submit-ios` (line 1032), plus `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (line 92),
   pinned the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`.
   That list also matches the labels advertised by the repo's Linux
   self-hosted box, so `Build iOS IPA` executed on Linux (`/home/runner/…`)
   with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode → `bundle: command not found` → `exit 127` at
   *Install fastlane* (run 38516656653); the 2026-10-15 night run
   additionally died on `security: command not found`. Same routing-bug
   class gh-1005 solved for `ci.yml` with the unique `macos-m5` label.
2. **Workspace isolation** — `bench-harbor.yml` wrote its harbor output
   INSIDE the build workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`,
   trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers). On the persistent
   self-hosted box the mobile legs' checkout ran a bare
   `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"`, which failed on the docker-held leftovers
   (`rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1) and failed the checkout before any
   build step.

**Impact**: every scheduled `daily-publish` TestFlight leg fails — no iOS
build ships; a bench run immediately followed by a mobile build on the same
box also breaks the checkout even when routing is fixed.

**Fix approach** (minimal, per the ticket's F-A/F-B; F-C is #1262's scope):

- **F-A**: pin all three macOS publish-leg jobs to
  `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique registration label of
  fa-m5-1, the repo's ONE self-hosted macOS runner (the exact convention
  ci.yml's `cube-kernel-live` already uses since gh-1005).
- **F-B (producer)**: bench-harbor writes its output to
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace
  path); the artifact + Harbor Hub uploads follow; a new `always()` step
  tears the shard's docker containers down BEFORE removing the output dir
  (both best-effort so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict).
- **F-B (consumer)**: all three mirror-checkout jobs (`build-ios`,
  `submit-ios`, `build-macos`) get the hardened clean INLINE — log-and-prune
  (removable paths removed; a still-blocked remainder moved aside into
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-workspace-*`; a surviving mount stub cloned around) —
  so a stale unremovable path can never fail the checkout. build-macos keeps
  its per-arch build cache park/restore, now best-effort (a lost cache
  rebuilds from scratch, never fails the checkout).
- **Why INLINE, not a composite action**: round 1 of this leg (WIP
  `ede8c5f3`) factored the checkout into
  `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` and consumed it via
  `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout`. That is incorrect on these
  runners: a local `./` action resolves against `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` AT STEP
  TIME, and on the persistent box that workspace is the PREVIOUS run's tree
  (or nothing) — the action file would be MISSING on the first post-merge
  run and silently STALE afterwards, because the checkout step is exactly
  the thing that materializes the tree. The inline scripts always execute
  the committed copy of the commit under test. (The action also assigned
  its `preserve-cache-dir` input single-quoted, keeping the caller's
  `$HOME` token literal — the cache would have parked in a junk
  `./'$HOME'/…` dir; the inline script's `BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/…"`
  expands natively.) The composite action is deleted.

**Previous attempt**: none merged — this is the first fix landed for
gh-1600 (a prior dev run 38733592508 saved WIP `ede8c5f3` but never
concluded; this round verified the WIP's intent, corrected its composite
action design, and completed verification).

## Verification

build-ios looks right. One consideration: `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` — a local composite action requires the action to exist in the checked-out tree... but the checkout happens VIA the action (chicken-and-egg!). On GitHub Actions, `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` resolves the action from the workspace — the runner needs the repo files at that point. {"content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1600 `[daily-publish] testflight leg failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: the `daily-publish` testflight leg failed through two independent
layers — (L1-routing) the iOS jobs routed onto the Linux self-hosted runner,
and (L1-isolation) the shared self-hosted workspace was polluted by bench
leftovers that broke the mirror-checkout.

**Root cause**:

1. **Routing** — `build-mobile.yml` jobs `build-ios` (line 605) and
   `submit-ios` (line 1032), plus `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (line 92),
   pinned the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`.
   That list also matches the labels advertised by the repo's Linux
   self-hosted box, so `Build iOS IPA` executed on Linux (`/home/runner/…`)
   with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode → `bundle: command not found` → `exit 127` at
   *Install fastlane* (run 38516656653); the 2026-10-15 night run
   additionally died on `security: command not found`. Same routing-bug
   class gh-1005 solved for `ci.yml` with the unique `macos-m5` label.
2. **Workspace isolation** — `bench-harbor.yml` wrote its harbor output
   INSIDE the build workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`,
   trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers). On the persistent
   self-hosted box the mobile legs' checkout ran a bare
   `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"`, which failed on the docker-held leftovers
   (`rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1) and failed the checkout before any
   build step.

**Impact**: every scheduled `daily-publish` TestFlight leg fails — no iOS
build ships; a bench run immediately followed by a mobile build on the same
box also breaks the checkout even when routing is fixed.

**Fix approach** (minimal, per the ticket's F-A/F-B; F-C is #1262's scope):

- **F-A**: pin all three macOS publish-leg jobs to
  `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique registration label of
  fa-m5-1, the repo's ONE self-hosted macOS runner (the exact convention
  ci.yml's `cube-kernel-live` already uses since gh-1005).
- **F-B (producer)**: bench-harbor writes its output to
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace
  path); the artifact + Harbor Hub uploads follow; a new `always()` step
  tears the shard's docker containers down BEFORE removing the output dir
  (both best-effort so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict).
- **F-B (consumer)**: all three mirror-checkout jobs (`build-ios`,
  `submit-ios`, `build-macos`) get the hardened clean INLINE — log-and-prune
  (removable paths removed; a still-blocked remainder moved aside into
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-workspace-*`; a surviving mount stub cloned around) —
  so a stale unremovable path can never fail the checkout. build-macos keeps
  its per-arch build cache park/restore, now best-effort (a lost cache
  rebuilds from scratch, never fails the checkout).
- **Why INLINE, not a composite action**: round 1 of this leg (WIP
  `ede8c5f3`) factored the checkout into
  `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` and consumed it via
  `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout`. That is incorrect on these
  runners: a local `./` action resolves against `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` AT STEP
  TIME, and on the persistent box that workspace is the PREVIOUS run's tree
  (or nothing) — the action file would be MISSING on the first post-merge
  run and silently STALE afterwards, because the checkout step is exactly
  the thing that materializes the tree. The inline scripts always execute
  the committed copy of the commit under test. (The action also assigned
  its `preserve-cache-dir` input single-quoted, keeping the caller's
  `$HOME` token literal — the cache would have parked in a junk
  `./'$HOME'/…` dir; the inline script's `BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/…"`
  expands natively.) The composite action is deleted.

**Previous attempt**: none merged — this is the first fix landed for
gh-1600 (a prior dev run 38733592508 saved WIP `ede8c5f3` but never
concluded; this round verified the WIP's intent, corrected its composite
action design, and completed verification).

## Verification

- RED: on `origin/main` the shape the regression test asserts is absent —
  `build-mobile.yml:605/1032` + `build-macos.yml:92` carry the generic
  `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` labels, `bench-harbor.yml:602/610` write
  `-o jobs` into the workspace, and no hardened clean exists — the
  reproduction test fails on base.
- GREEN: `dart test test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — 10 tests
  pass (AC1 runner-pin asserts + AC2 isolation asserts, incl. the audit
  that NO self-hosted job in either leg skips the `macos-m5` pin, the
  no-local-action assert, and the cache-park-before-clean assert).

On GitHub Actions, `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` resolves the action from the workspace — the runner needs the repo files at that point. In the ORIGINAL flow, the checkout was a `run:` step that cloned into `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` manually — the workspace at step time was the (nearly) empty shared dir, NOT a Actions-checkout-populated tree.

GitHub's composite action resolution reads `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/actions/mirror-checkout` — if the workspace is empty (the persistent-box scenario), the action file DOESN'T EXIST → the step fails with "Can't find 'action.yml'".

GitHub docs: "Path to the directory containing the action, relative to the repository's root" — for jobs that don't run actions/checkout first, a local action can't be used (docs say local actions only run after checkout in the SAME job... actually the requirement is the files exist in the workspace).

In build-ios, the first step updates the mirror (run step), second step is the composite action — at that point the workspace on the persistent runner is... whatever the PREVIOUS run left there! Because these jobs deliberately do NOT use actions/checkout — they hand-clone via mirror. On a hosted runner the workspace starts empty → `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` would FAIL (no such file).

On the shared self-hosted runner, the workspace holds the previous run's checkout (the previous workflow that ran there — could be ANY workflow, e.g. an old commit of the repo that may pre-date the action). So:

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1600 `[daily-publish] testflight leg failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: the `daily-publish` testflight leg failed through two independent
layers — (L1-routing) the iOS jobs routed onto the Linux self-hosted runner,
and (L1-isolation) the shared self-hosted workspace was polluted by bench
leftovers that broke the mirror-checkout.

**Root cause**:

1. **Routing** — `build-mobile.yml` jobs `build-ios` (line 605) and
   `submit-ios` (line 1032), plus `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (line 92),
   pinned the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`.
   That list also matches the labels advertised by the repo's Linux
   self-hosted box, so `Build iOS IPA` executed on Linux (`/home/runner/…`)
   with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode → `bundle: command not found` → `exit 127` at
   *Install fastlane* (run 38516656653); the 2026-10-15 night run
   additionally died on `security: command not found`. Same routing-bug
   class gh-1005 solved for `ci.yml` with the unique `macos-m5` label.
2. **Workspace isolation** — `bench-harbor.yml` wrote its harbor output
   INSIDE the build workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`,
   trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers). On the persistent
   self-hosted box the mobile legs' checkout ran a bare
   `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"`, which failed on the docker-held leftovers
   (`rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1) and failed the checkout before any
   build step.

**Impact**: every scheduled `daily-publish` TestFlight leg fails — no iOS
build ships; a bench run immediately followed by a mobile build on the same
box also breaks the checkout even when routing is fixed.

**Fix approach** (minimal, per the ticket's F-A/F-B; F-C is #1262's scope):

- **F-A**: pin all three macOS publish-leg jobs to
  `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique registration label of
  fa-m5-1, the repo's ONE self-hosted macOS runner (the exact convention
  ci.yml's `cube-kernel-live` already uses since gh-1005).
- **F-B (producer)**: bench-harbor writes its output to
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace
  path); the artifact + Harbor Hub uploads follow; a new `always()` step
  tears the shard's docker containers down BEFORE removing the output dir
  (both best-effort so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict).
- **F-B (consumer)**: all three mirror-checkout jobs (`build-ios`,
  `submit-ios`, `build-macos`) get the hardened clean INLINE — log-and-prune
  (removable paths removed; a still-blocked remainder moved aside into
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-workspace-*`; a surviving mount stub cloned around) —
  so a stale unremovable path can never fail the checkout. build-macos keeps
  its per-arch build cache park/restore, now best-effort (a lost cache
  rebuilds from scratch, never fails the checkout).
- **Why INLINE, not a composite action**: round 1 of this leg (WIP
  `ede8c5f3`) factored the checkout into
  `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` and consumed it via
  `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout`. That is incorrect on these
  runners: a local `./` action resolves against `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` AT STEP
  TIME, and on the persistent box that workspace is the PREVIOUS run's tree
  (or nothing) — the action file would be MISSING on the first post-merge
  run and silently STALE afterwards, because the checkout step is exactly
  the thing that materializes the tree. The inline scripts always execute
  the committed copy of the commit under test. (The action also assigned
  its `preserve-cache-dir` input single-quoted, keeping the caller's
  `$HOME` token literal — the cache would have parked in a junk
  `./'$HOME'/…` dir; the inline script's `BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/…"`
  expands natively.) The composite action is deleted.

**Previous attempt**: none merged — this is the first fix landed for
gh-1600 (a prior dev run 38733592508 saved WIP `ede8c5f3` but never
concluded; this round verified the WIP's intent, corrected its composite
action design, and completed verification).

## Verification

- RED: on `origin/main` the shape the regression test asserts is absent —
  `build-mobile.yml:605/1032` + `build-macos.yml:92` carry the generic
  `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` labels, `bench-harbor.yml:602/610` write
  `-o jobs` into the workspace, and no hardened clean exists — the
  reproduction test fails on base.
- GREEN: `dart test test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — 10 tests
  pass (AC1 runner-pin asserts + AC2 isolation asserts, incl. the audit
  that NO self-hosted job in either leg skips the `macos-m5` pin, the
  no-local-action assert, and the cache-park-before-clean assert).
- Behavioral sim of the REAL committed scripts (extracted from the workflow
  YAML and executed in a sandbox with a fake local mirror), 3 modes: clean
  clone; build-macos cache parked under the expanded `$HOME` + restored
  (with no junk literal-`$HOME` dir); surviving-stub clone-around with the
  remainder moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP` — all pass. Embedded scripts pass
  `bash -n`; all touched YAML parses.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (fresh run against the
  final tree — see response.md for the final count).

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1600 `[daily-publish] testflight leg failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: the `daily-publish` testflight leg failed through two independent
layers — (L1-routing) the iOS jobs routed onto the Linux self-hosted runner,
and (L1-isolation) the shared self-hosted workspace was polluted by bench
leftovers that broke the mirror-checkout.

**Root cause**:

1. **Routing** — `build-mobile.yml` jobs `build-ios` (line 605) and
   `submit-ios` (line 1032), plus `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (line 92),
   pinned the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`.
   That list also matches the labels advertised by the repo's Linux
   self-hosted box, so `Build iOS IPA` executed on Linux (`/home/runner/…`)
   with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode → `bundle: command not found` → `exit 127` at
   *Install fastlane* (run 38516656653); the 2026-10-15 night run
   additionally died on `security: command not found`. Same routing-bug
   class gh-1005 solved for `ci.yml` with the unique `macos-m5` label.
2. **Workspace isolation** — `bench-harbor.yml` wrote its harbor output
   INSIDE the build workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`,
   trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers). On the persistent
   self-hosted box the mobile legs' checkout ran a bare
   `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"`, which failed on the docker-held leftovers
   (`rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1) and failed the checkout before any
   build step.

**Impact**: every scheduled `daily-publish` TestFlight leg fails — no iOS
build ships; a bench run immediately followed by a mobile build on the same
box also breaks the checkout even when routing is fixed.

**Fix approach** (minimal, per the ticket's F-A/F-B; F-C is #1262's scope):

- **F-A**: pin all three macOS publish-leg jobs to
  `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique registration label of
  fa-m5-1, the repo's ONE self-hosted macOS runner (the exact convention
  ci.yml's `cube-kernel-live` already uses since gh-1005).
- **F-B (producer)**: bench-harbor writes its output to
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace
  path); the artifact + Harbor Hub uploads follow; a new `always()` step
  tears the shard's docker containers down BEFORE removing the output dir
  (both best-effort so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict).
- **F-B (consumer)**: all three mirror-checkout jobs (`build-ios`,
  `submit-ios`, `build-macos`) get the hardened clean INLINE — log-and-prune
  (removable paths removed; a still-blocked remainder moved aside into
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-workspace-*`; a surviving mount stub cloned around) —
  so a stale unremovable path can never fail the checkout. build-macos keeps
  its per-arch build cache park/restore, now best-effort (a lost cache
  rebuilds from scratch, never fails the checkout).
- **Why INLINE, not a composite action**: round 1 of this leg (WIP
  `ede8c5f3`) factored the checkout into
  `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` and consumed it via
  `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout`. That is incorrect on these
  runners: a local `./` action resolves against `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` AT STEP
  TIME, and on the persistent box that workspace is the PREVIOUS run's tree
  (or nothing) — the action file would be MISSING on the first post-merge
  run and silently STALE afterwards, because the checkout step is exactly
  the thing that materializes the tree. The inline scripts always execute
  the committed copy of the commit under test. (The action also assigned
  its `preserve-cache-dir` input single-quoted, keeping the caller's
  `$HOME` token literal — the cache would have parked in a junk
  `./'$HOME'/…` dir; the inline script's `BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/…"`
  expands natively.) The composite action is deleted.

**Previous attempt**: none merged — this is the first fix landed for
gh-1600 (a prior dev run 38733592508 saved WIP `ede8c5f3` but never
concluded; this round verified the WIP's intent, corrected its composite
action design, and completed verification).

## Verification

- RED: on `origin/main` the shape the regression test asserts is absent —
  `build-mobile.yml:605/1032` + `build-macos.yml:92` carry the generic
  `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` labels, `bench-harbor.yml:602/610` write
  `-o jobs` into the workspace, and no hardened clean exists — the
  reproduction test fails on base.
- GREEN: `dart test test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — 10 tests
  pass (AC1 runner-pin asserts + AC2 isolation asserts, incl. the audit
  that NO self-hosted job in either leg skips the `macos-m5` pin, the
  no-local-action assert, and the cache-park-before-clean assert).
- Behavioral sim of the REAL committed scripts (extracted from the workflow
  YAML and executed in a sandbox with a fake local mirror), 3 modes: clean
  clone; build-macos cache parked under the expanded `$HOME` + restored
  (with no junk literal-`$HOME` dir); surviving-stub clone-around with the
  remainder moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP` — all pass. Embedded scripts pass
  `bash -n`; all touched YAML parses.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (fresh run against the
  final tree — see response.md for the final count).

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1600 `[daily-publish] testflight leg failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: the `daily-publish` testflight leg failed through two independent
layers — (L1-routing) the iOS jobs routed onto the Linux self-hosted runner,
and (L1-isolation) the shared self-hosted workspace was polluted by bench
leftovers that broke the mirror-checkout.

**Root cause**:

1. **Routing** — `build-mobile.yml` jobs `build-ios` (line 605) and
   `submit-ios` (line 1032), plus `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (line 92),
   pinned the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`.
   That list also matches the labels advertised by the repo's Linux
   self-hosted box, so `Build iOS IPA` executed on Linux (`/home/runner/…`)
   with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode → `bundle: command not found` → `exit 127` at
   *Install fastlane* (run 38516656653); the 2026-10-15 night run
   additionally died on `security: command not found`. Same routing-bug
   class gh-1005 solved for `ci.yml` with the unique `macos-m5` label.
2. **Workspace isolation** — `bench-harbor.yml` wrote its harbor output
   INSIDE the build workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`,
   trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers). On the persistent
   self-hosted box the mobile legs' checkout ran a bare
   `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"`, which failed on the docker-held leftovers
   (`rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1) and failed the checkout before any
   build step.

**Impact**: every scheduled `daily-publish` TestFlight leg fails — no iOS
build ships; a bench run immediately followed by a mobile build on the same
box also breaks the checkout even when routing is fixed.

**Fix approach** (minimal, per the ticket's F-A/F-B; F-C is #1262's scope):

- **F-A**: pin all three macOS publish-leg jobs to
  `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique registration label of
  fa-m5-1, the repo's ONE self-hosted macOS runner (the exact convention
  ci.yml's `cube-kernel-live` already uses since gh-1005).
- **F-B (producer)**: bench-harbor writes its output to
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace
  path); the artifact + Harbor Hub uploads follow; a new `always()` step
  tears the shard's docker containers down BEFORE removing the output dir
  (both best-effort so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict).
- **F-B (consumer)**: all three mirror-checkout jobs (`build-ios`,
  `submit-ios`, `build-macos`) get the hardened clean INLINE — log-and-prune
  (removable paths removed; a still-blocked remainder moved aside into
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-workspace-*`; a surviving mount stub cloned around) —
  so a stale unremovable path can never fail the checkout. build-macos keeps
  its per-arch build cache park/restore, now best-effort (a lost cache
  rebuilds from scratch, never fails the checkout).
- **Why INLINE, not a composite action**: round 1 of this leg (WIP
  `ede8c5f3`) factored the checkout into
  `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` and consumed it via
  `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout`. That is incorrect on these
  runners: a local `./` action resolves against `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` AT STEP
  TIME, and on the persistent box that workspace is the PREVIOUS run's tree
  (or nothing) — the action file would be MISSING on the first post-merge
  run and silently STALE afterwards, because the checkout step is exactly
  the thing that materializes the tree. The inline scripts always execute
  the committed copy of the commit under test. (The action also assigned
  its `preserve-cache-dir` input single-quoted, keeping the caller's
  `$HOME` token literal — the cache would have parked in a junk
  `./'$HOME'/…` dir; the inline script's `BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/…"`
  expands natively.) The composite action is deleted.

**Previous attempt**: none merged — this is the first fix landed for
gh-1600 (a prior dev run 38733592508 saved WIP `ede8c5f3` but never
concluded; this round verified the WIP's intent, corrected its composite
action design, and completed verification).

## Verification

- RED: on `origin/main` the shape the regression test asserts is absent —
  `build-mobile.yml:605/1032` + `build-macos.yml:92` carry the generic
  `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` labels, `bench-harbor.yml:602/610` write
  `-o jobs` into the workspace, and no hardened clean exists — the
  reproduction test fails on base.
